title: 12-layer ZnS/ZnSe stack with geometric progression initialization and constrained step size
scientific_hypothesis: A linear geometric progression in layer thickness (350-950 nm across 12 layers) anchors the macroscopic optical phase slope, enabling the optimizer to resolve finer interference features between MWIR suppression and LWIR transmission bands rather than leaping across spectral resonances.
design_principle: Thickness gradient creates distributed phase accumulation that separates MWIR stopband from LWIR passband more cleanly than uniform initialization. Constrained step size (±80 nm) prevents large jumps that skip local optima.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | Ge substrate (12 finite layers, alternating starting with ZnS)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses (12 optimizable variables, bounds 300-1000 nm)
Initialization: linear progression from 350 nm to 950 nm
Optimizer max step: ±80 nm per iteration
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize average transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain smooth spectral transition between bands
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 300-1000 nm compatible with thermal evaporation
Alternating ZnS/ZnSe sequence simplifies deposition scheduling
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for dichroic filter design
Interference phase accumulation in multilayer systems
Gradient-based optimization with step constraints for spectral feature resolution
expected_advantages: Improved separation of MWIR/LWIR bands through distributed phase control
Reduced risk of optimizer skipping local optima
Better convergence stability compared to uniform initialization
known_risks: Geometric progression may not match optimal quarter-wave conditions at either band center
Step constraint may slow convergence if initial guess is far from optimum
12 layers may be insufficient for deep MWIR suppression
execution_request_english: Design a 12-layer planar multilayer dielectric film on Ge substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe (12 finite layers total, alternating starting with ZnS at air interface). All 12 layer thicknesses are optimizable variables with bounds 300-1000 nm. Initialize thicknesses with linear geometric progression: layer 1 = 350 nm, layer 12 = 950 nm, intermediate layers linearly interpolated. Constrain optimizer maximum single-step displacement to ±80 nm per iteration. Use coherent TMM solver at normal incidence (0 degrees), unpolarized light. Spectral range: 3000-11000 nm with 2001 sample points. Objective: maximize average transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band while minimizing average transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 12 (within 16-layer manufacturing constraint). Materials resolved via registry (ZnS, ZnSe, Ge). Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 8000-11000 nm, 3000-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band; Low transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count not exceeding 16.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: replaced near-uniform ~750 nm initialization with linear geometric progression (350-950 nm) and added ±80 nm step constraint to anchor macroscopic phase slope and force finer interference feature resolution. Previous 12-layer route_03 variants used frozen outer layers or uniform initialization which showed score regression.
